dedupe_keys.name: x iiotid connectivity and device agnostic intrusion dataset for the industrial internet of things

description: X-IIoTID is an intrusion dataset for Industrial Internet of Things systems. The IEEE DataPort page says it reproduces recent attacker tactics, techniques and procedures alongside realistic IIoT activity, including control loop devices (sensors, actuators and controllers), edge, mobile and cloud traffic, protocols such as MQTT, CoAP and WebSocket and machine-to-machine and human-to-machine communication; features come from network traffic, system and application logs, device resources and the OSSEC and Zeek intrusion detection logs. The final version has 820,834 instances (421,417 normal and 399,417 attack) with 68 features and three label levels. It was submitted by Muna Al-Hawawreh, Elena Sitnikova and Neda Aboutorab of UNSW Canberra and last updated in May 2022, as one CSV zip of about 107 MB. DataCite gives the licence as CC BY 4.0, but the page marks it a Standard Dataset, so files need an IEEE DataPort subscription (US$40 a month, free for IEEE Society members). Coverage is one emulated IIoT testbed. Caveats: it is a lab testbed, and the attack mix reflects the authors' design. For simulation it gives labelled multi-source attack records to test intrusion detection before cyber attacks reach plant control models. Related catalogue records include the IIoT false data injection dataset and ICS-ADD.
